rationale: 'complete' on a work item means the handler saga returned success, not that the defect is gone. CLAUDE.md already enshrines this rule ('Trust the rendered artefact, not the status. complete is not proof the work happened') and the platform has already been bitten by it: robot-hands' gripper-detail product sections were marked complete on 2026-07-10 and were still serving empty markup on 2026-07-14. The fix for that case was built and is good — verifiers.go plus the completion gate in complete_work_item_verification.go, which consults a per-item_type verifier before stamping complete and routes a failed verification into the attempt machinery. But only ONE verifier has ever been registered: RegisterVerifier("empty_section", ...) in check_empty_sections.go:38. Live consequence, 2026-07-18: of 4,599 complete items, exactly 5 carry a result._verification record, and 9 items have ever reached 'verified' — all of them empty_section, none since 2026-07-14. So a working, tested, already-wired safety mechanism is covering roughly one item type out of fifty, and every other item type still self-reports. This submission registers verifiers for three more item types whose defect predicate is a cheap deterministic re-check, reusing each check's own predicate so detection and verification cannot drift. Secondary motivation, stated so reviewers can weigh it: the reasoning-dataset workstream needs ground-truth outcome labels, and a verified/regressed distinction is worth far more as a training label than a self-reported complete — but the platform-quality argument stands on its own and is the reason to do it.

plan.summary: The completion-time verification framework is built, wired and proven, but has one verifier registered out of ~50 item types, so 4,594 of 4,599 complete items were never checked. Register verifiers for three more item types (hardcoded_section_colors, phantom_internal_link, image_url_404) by extracting each existing discovery check's predicate into a shared pure function that both the check and the new verifier call, so the two can never diverge. No new tables, no schema change, no new LLM spend.

edits.rationale: Highest-volume item type with a purely deterministic predicate (7 complete / 3 detected / 2 unresolved live). The check already knows how to decide whether a component carries hardcoded colours; the verifier asks the same question of the same component after the fix. Following the empty_section precedent exactly, including its 'row is gone means resolved' branch, so a deleted component reads as fixed rather than erroring.

Deterministic and cheap: the defect is 'this internal link points at a target that does not resolve', which is a DB lookup. This file already has a test (check_phantom_internal_links_test.go), so the extracted predicate has somewhere to be tested without new scaffolding.

The only one of the three whose predicate leaves the database (an HTTP check), which makes its failure modes different and worth calling out rather than hiding: a transient network error must return an error, NOT Resolved:false. The completion gate's documented policy is to fail OPEN on verifier error (complete, recording the error under result._verification), so an error is safe while a false 'not resolved' would wrongly push a genuinely fixed item into the retry/attempt machinery.

The file's comment explains the mechanism but not that registration is opt-in per item_type, which is precisely the assumption that left it at one verifier for months. Naming the gap where the next author will read it is what stops this recurring — the same structural argument bugs_open/016 makes about seat growth.

grounded_in: platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/check_empty_sections.go:38 — RegisterVerifier("empty_section", VerifyEmptySectionResolved) — the only RegisterVerifier call in the codebase.

platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/verifiers.go:47-51 — "RegisterVerifier adds a verifier for an item_type. Called from init() in check files, alongside Register(check)." — the mechanism is built and documented; only the calls are missing.

platform/orchestration/actions/complete_work_item_verification.go:14-21 — "no verifier registered for the item_type -> complete as before ... verifier errors -> fail OPEN (complete, recording the error under result._verification) ... verifier says the defect persists -> do NOT complete; route into the same attempt machinery as fail_work_item".
Live DB 2026-07-18: SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE result ? '_verification') FROM site_work_items WHERE status='complete' — 4599 complete, 5 with a verification record.
Live DB 2026-07-18: SELECT item_type, count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE status='verified' GROUP BY 1 — empty_section 9, max created_at 2026-07-14. No other item_type has ever been verified.

platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/verifiers.go:17-19 — "An ItemVerifier answers 'is the defect this item describes actually gone?' at completion time, re-using the SAME predicate the discovery check used to create the item." — this plan's shared-predicate extraction is the stated design intent, not a new idea.
plan.risks: The real risk is a verifier that is WRONG in the strict direction: returning Resolved:false for an item that is actually fixed pushes it into the attempt machinery, burns an attempt, and at max_attempts lands it in 'failed' — turning a fixed defect into a permanent false negative. That is why each sketch reuses the detection predicate rather than restating the rule, and why image_url_404 returns an error (fail open) rather than false on any transport failure. A reviewer should check each predicate for that asymmetry specifically. Second risk: the extraction refactor changes detection behaviour as a side effect — the extracted function must be behaviour-identical to the inline predicate it replaces, and check_phantom_internal_links_test.go / check_empty_sections_test.go are the existing pattern for locking that. Third: image_url_404's verifier makes an outbound HTTP request on the completion path, adding latency to every completion of that item type; it must be bounded by the passed ctx and should not retry. Scope note: this adds verifiers only. It deliberately does NOT stamp status='verified' (no Go code sets that on site_work_items today, and introducing a new terminal status would touch the workItemTerminalStatuses / idx_swi_dedup lockstep that has caused fleet-wide 42P10 before). The verification evidence lands in result._verification, which is additive and already read by nothing that would break.
